chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: The 1923 show Steppin' High and the band behind it
summary: Reb's American Legion Club band was originally Seven Pods of Pepper; Steppin' High featured the Spikes brothers' songs, was staged by Smith and Petrie at the Philharmonic, and went east.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Reb's American Legion Club 45s--that was the name of the band?
No, that was the name of the club. We just called it that 'cause we played over there, I think, Saturdays and Sundays. But that was originally what we called "Seven Pods of Pepper."
You had a singer with your band at one point called Herman Higgs?
Herman Higgs, yeah.
On the show, "Steppin' High," that was in the year...what?
1923. And you wrote...the book by Billy Pierson and the music and lyrics by John C. Spikes and Benjamin F. Spikes.
Yeah.
And the tunes...
He didn't have any book. He...every time we'd

bring a song, he'd write a...somthing to bring uh...uh...in a...in the show to fit the song.
That's an interesting way to work.
Yeah.
And this was done...uh, the show was produced...
The show was produced. It went all the way back to New York. Yeah.
Oh. But it was first produced where? Here?

Produced here. I think Paul Whi...I think Paul Howard was with it. They...see, they...the Black and Tan...uh, uh, uh... no, I think they were the...I don't know whether they called themselves the Black and Tan or the Quality...uh, uh...
Serenaders?
Quality Serenaders. They went back with it. I think Paul Whiteman...Paul...
Howard.
...Howard was with them, and Harvey Brooks, and I think they all went back to New York.
Mmmmm hmmmmm. So it starred comedian Strawberry Russell. Right?
Yeah.

And you were just--when I was turning on the tape, you said that these songs listed on the front of the sheet music--"My Mammy's Blues," "Love, Love, Why Do You Seem So Hard To Hold?" "The Whole World Seems Wrong," "The Charleston Craze," "Drifting Back Home," "Sunshine

Reel 5

May," "What'll You Do?" and "You're Not The Only One That's Lonesome." Those were...
Those were specialty songs in the show--plus we had all the other openings and choruses to things that...to write, you know.
Mmmm hmmm. How long did the show run?
A regular show--two hours, you know. Stage show.
And it started here. Did it play any place along the way between here and...
All the way from here to New York...I think. Now, I don't know. I don't remember but the people that own the Philharmonic Auditorium put it on at that time. Petrie and them. Doesn't it say on there.
Yes, it says, "Direction...Smith & Petrie."
Yeah. See, they ran the uh...the uh...the Philharmonic Auditorium at that time, and they produced the show.
I see. So it started at the Philharmonic, and it went back...where'd it play in New York?
I don't know after it left here; I know that soon as they got to New York, they...wasn't long before they was back here.
